title: Power Platform: secure Dataverse records with column-based filtering
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, preview access model and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should clarify the existing product licensing, complete the security-role path, name the API request properties and add supporting citations.

claims.claim: The planned enhancement secures Dataverse records using column attribute values rather than traditional ownership.
claims.quote: This enhancement introduces column-based security filtering, enabling records to be secured using attribute values rather than traditional ownership.

claims.claim: Security administrators can define access by business dimensions such as region or department.
claims.quote: This allows security admins to define access based on business dimensions such as region or department

claims.claim: Reporting and aggregated datasets without natural record ownership are intended scenarios.
claims.quote: making it ideal for scenarios where record ownership does not exist—such as reporting and aggregated datasets.

claims.claim: The planned approach removes artificial ownership or complex sharing models and simplifies administration at scale.
claims.quote: By eliminating the need for artificial ownership or complex sharing models, this approach simplifies security administration, improves scalability

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions

claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability", "Preview" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-11-11T00:56:01.
Microsoft Learn documents filter-based security as a preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview.

claims.claim: Record Filters use FetchXML to identify qualifying records.
claims.quote: Record Filter: Uses FetchXML to identify records that qualify for access.

claims.claim: Entity Record Filters associate Record Filters with Dataverse tables.
claims.quote: Entity Record Filter: Associates a Record Filter with a Dataverse table.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Filter privileges are granted through security roles.
claims.quote: When you associate a filter with a table, Dataverse creates filter privileges. Assign these privileges through security roles.

claims.claim: Tables can use filtered record ownership without record owners.
claims.quote: Filtered record ownership is a Dataverse ownership model that determines access entirely through filter privileges. Filtered ownership tables don't use record owners.

claims.claim: Filters can also be added to existing user, team or organization record ownership tables.
claims.quote: You can apply filter-based security to user or team, and organization record ownership, and filtered record ownership tables.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: On user-owned tables, filter privileges add access and never reduce existing ownership-based access.
claims.quote: For user or team record ownership tables, filter privileges add row-level access to ownership-based security. They don't replace or reduce access granted through ownership, sharing, or security role privileges.

claims.claim: Records in filtered ownership tables cannot be shared.
claims.quote: Can't be shared with users or teams.

claims.claim: Records in filtered ownership tables cannot be assigned.
claims.quote: Can't be assigned to users or teams.

claims.claim: Creating a filtered ownership table automatically grants its All records filter privilege to System Administrator.
claims.quote: When you create a filtered record ownership table, Dataverse creates a global All records filter privilege and grants it to the System Administrator security role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Effective filter access combines privileges from users' security roles and team memberships.
claims.quote: Dataverse combines all authorized filters from the user's security roles and team memberships. A record that matches any authorized filter receives the corresponding access.

claims.claim: The System Administrator security role is required to configure the preview feature and its security roles.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles.

claims.claim: Admin-opt-in describes the control: an administrator must configure filters and grant their privileges through security roles.
claims.quote: A user with the system administrator security role must configure the feature and security roles. ... After creating the record filter and entity record filter, grant the filter for the required Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, or Append to table privileges in a security role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing Dataverse table licensing requirements apply.
claims.quote: App makers can use most of the tables available within Microsoft Dataverse (including custom tables and tables that are part of the Common Data Model) to create apps and flows for users who have a Power Apps or Power Automate license.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown, with no feature-specific licence published.
claims.quote: Users can create custom tables with Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and replace licensing.notes with 'Existing Dataverse table licensing applies: users can create custom tables with a Dynamics 365, Power Apps, or Power Automate license. No licence specific to filter-based security is published as of November 2026.' The cited table-licensing page gives the product-level requirement, not a separate feature entitlement.

claims.claim: No separate licence or licence change specific to filter-based security is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse filtered record ownership licensing price general availability capacity; "filtered record ownership" "license" "pricing". Read feature admin, maker and developer pages and License requirements for tables; none names a separate feature licence.

claims.claim: Feature-specific general availability pricing is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse filtered record ownership licensing price general availability capacity; "filtered record ownership" "license" "pricing". Read the feature guides, table licensing and capacity-storage pages; no feature-specific GA price was stated.

claims.claim: Dataverse capacity applies to the tables used by the feature.
claims.quote: Dataverse - Database capacity: Tracks structured data stored directly in Dataverse, including table rows, metadata, and relational data created by Power Apps, Power Automate, Dynamics 365 customer engagement apps

claims.claim: Power Apps provides environment > Solutions > solution > New table > Table (advanced properties) > Record ownership > Filtered (preview).
claims.quote: Select your environment. ... Go to Solutions, open the solution you want or create a new one. ... Select New table on the command bar, and then select Table (advanced properties). ... From the Record ownership list, select Filtered (preview).

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters creates a Record Filter, not a table.
claims.quote: Create a recordfilter row. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/recordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... "fetchxml": "<fetch><entity name=\"new_store\"><filter type=\"and\">
claims.fix: Remove ', each with a request body' from controls[0].api.call and the rendered call. Add to the row note: 'The recordfilters request body sets fetchxml.' Keep the documented POST endpoint unchanged.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters associates a Record Filter with a table rather than creating a table.
claims.quote: Use the RecordFilterId single-valued navigation property to associate the record filter. ... POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/entityrecordfilters HTTP/1.1 ... "objecttypecode": "new_store", "RecordFilterId@odata.bind": "/recordfilters(
claims.fix: Keep the documented entityrecordfilters POST endpoint and add to controls[0].note: 'The entityrecordfilters request body sets objecttypecode to the table logical name and RecordFilterId@odata.bind to the Record Filter.'

claims.claim: Within a Power Apps solution, + New > More > Other > Record Filter creates a Record Filter separately from the table.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions and create a new solution or open an existing solution. ... Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select Record Filter.

claims.claim: EntityRecordFilter is the separate solution component used to associate the created filter with a table.
claims.quote: Return to your Solution. ... Select + New. ... Select More and Other. ... Select EntityRecordFilter. ... Select the Record Filter ... Enter the Related Entity, the logical name of the table

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > role reaches the role whose filter privileges are configured.
claims.quote: Select Manage on the navigation pane. ... select Environments and then select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Users + permissions and select Security roles. ... Choose the security role you want to edit.
claims.fix: Complete the path in front matter and the rendered table as 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > role > target table > filter privilege'. The last two selections are documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/filter-based-security#grant-filter-privileges-in-security-roles; the current path stops early on the correct role page.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole adds existing privileges using a Privileges collection of RolePrivilege values.
claims.quote: Pass the list as the AddPrivilegesRole.Privileges parameter. ... POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(44ee44ee-ff55-aa66-bb77-88cc88cc88cc)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole HTTP/1.1
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/web-api-functions-actions-sample#section-8-bound-action-addprivilegesrole to sources for the full versioned invocation. Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<roleid>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole' and move 'The request body supplies a Privileges collection of RolePrivilege values' to the note. The cited AddPrivilegesRole reference confirms the bound action and parameter; the pre-check's missing literal POST text is not an invalid endpoint.

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterId property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterId | Edm.Guid | The Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: RolePrivilege has a RecordFilterUniqueName property.
claims.quote: RecordFilterUniqueName | Edm.String | The Unique Name for the Record Filter of the privilege.

claims.claim: Record Filters and Entity Record Filters are solution components.
claims.quote: An unmanaged solution and its unique name. All solution components created by the examples are associated with this solution. ... createRecordFilterRequest["SolutionUniqueName"] ... createEntityRecordFilterRequest["SolutionUniqueName"]

claims.claim: These solution components can travel with solutions through application lifecycle management deployments.
claims.quote: Solutions are the mechanism for implementing application lifecycle management (ALM) in Power Apps and Power Automate. ... The purpose of having components is ... so that it can be exported, imported
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/alm/solution-concepts-alm to sources for the existing statement that solution components can travel with solutions through ALM deployments.
